newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Vencemos to remain under Cemex control.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Vencemos to remain under Cemex control.

text.p: Venezuelan cement company Vencemos is to remain under the control of Mexican cement giant Cemex, but via Spanish Cemex affiliate Valenciana Cementos, Vencemos President Francisco Garza told Reuters.

Valenciana said Tuesday it was negotiating a multi-currency syndicated loan of 108.4 billion pesetas ($852.4 million) to buy Vencemos and U.S. cement maker Sunbelt Corp. Both are part of the Cemex group.
The purchase "is only part of the group's internal financial strategy. The administrative part remains unchanged," Garza said in a brief telephone interview.
Garza added, however, he would remain company president until December 1, and would then work directly for Cemex in Mexico. Venezuelan Victor Romo would subsequently assume the Vencemos presidency.
Vencemos, which has 4.5 million tonne production capacity, reported nine-month net profits of 35.4 billion bolivars ($75 million) versus 21.9 billion ($46.6 million) over the same period in 1995.
Cemex said the third quarter results represented a drop in gross margins "due to the high ratio of export sales to national sales."
